framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
clause_or_page: EC AI Act policy page, 'Application timeline' paragraph
requirement_paraphrase: Commission page states the Act became applicable on 2 August 2026 with exceptions: prohibitions and AI literacy from 2 Feb 2025; governance and GPAI obligations from 2 Aug 2025; Annex I high-risk to 2 Aug 2028; Annex III to 2 Dec 2027; AI Omnibus political agreement 7 May 2026, in force 27 July 2026.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems conforming to harmonised standards (or parts) whose references are published in the OJ are presumed to meet the Section 2 requirements to the extent the standards cover them.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Member States may allow real-world testing outside sandboxes of AI-enabled products under Annex I Section B legislation, through national frameworks that require a mandatory testing plan agreed with the authority and apply most Art. 60 safeguards.
what_is_tested: Real-world testing of Section B products

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.
what_is_tested: Pre-market and periodic testing of AI-content marking and detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Safety mitigations must be robust under adversarial pressure, and signatories carry out post-market monitoring (feedback channels, incident forms, bug bounties and similar) to inform whether the risk stays acceptable.

Technical report surveying how trust in AI can be built through transparency, explainability and controllability, engineering pitfalls and threats, and approaches to assessing and improving properties such as resilience, safety, security and privacy; does not define trustworthiness levels; published 28 May 2020, 43 pages.

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct a cybersecurity risk assessment that classifies AI agents' actions by potential impact, likelihood and reversibility, and apply appropriate safeguards.
what_is_tested: Cybersecurity risk of AI agent actions

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (version read: v1.0, 22 Jan 2026; v1.5 not read)
requirement_paraphrase: Test in real or realistic environments that mirror production (balancing realism against risk of real-world side effects), test repeatedly across varied datasets to observe low-probability behaviours and stability, and evaluate results at scale using different methods per workflow part; the source describes current industry solutions as LLM or agent evaluators, or human evaluation (practice described, not a recommendation).

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations Reg 10 / Commissioner materials Accreditation and Certification Framework
clause_or_page: D p.5 'Why is the Framework necessary?'; p.4
requirement_paraphrase: Framework says the Regulations bar commercial use of Systems for High Risk Processing unless audit and certification requirements are met; applicant defined as 'Certification Applicant'.
what_is_tested: Compliance of High Risk Processing Systems with certification requirements

framework: Dubai Department of Finance AI Policy (Arabic)
requirement_paraphrase: The Department commits to identify, assess and manage risks of its AI systems (technical, regulatory, ethical, bias, misuse) and to feed impact assessment results into risk management.
what_is_tested: Risks of the Department's AI systems

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Security risks > Using AI > Data and model poisoning
requirement_paraphrase: To counter data and model poisoning, model outputs should be tested against known good responses and systematically tested for bias.
what_is_tested: Output integrity against known-good responses; bias
who_tests: Not specified (passive voice); context refers to the organisation running the model

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Design the evaluation protocol, write evaluation code, run and track results, and debug the evaluation; common bugs include degraded serving; evaluation cheating and evaluation awareness are listed as bugs tagged [Emerging Practice].
